title: OLS Assumptions – definitions, consequences and mitigations
text: OLS Assumptions – definitions, consequences and mitigations Assumptions Consequences of violations Mitigations Linearity Misspecification errors Variable transformation (log, dummy variables, higher order terms, …) Homoscedasticity (Constant Variance of Errors) Unreliable test results (t test and F test) Estimating separate models for each sub- sample, variable transformation, interaction terms, … No Perfect Multicollinearity No unique solutions. High multicollinearity causes biased coefficient estimates and inflated standard errors. Removal of variables. Independence (No Autocorrelation) Biased coefficient estimates Misleading test results Usually only a concern when using time series data. First differencing is routinely used to address this issue. 𝜀~𝑁0, 𝑎: The error term is normally distributed with a zero mean Unreliable test results (t test and F test) This assumption is less critical when the sample size is large due to the Central Limit Theorem, and the model contains an intercept term.

title: OLS Assumptions and Standard Diagnostic Tests
text: OLS Assumptions and Standard Diagnostic Tests Assumptions Standard Tests STATA commands Linearity Scatter plots or residual plots, RESET test twoway scatter ovtest Homoscedasticity (Constant Variance of Errors) Residual plots (residuals vs. fitted values), White Test, … twoway scatter estat hettest No Perfect Multicollinearity No need to test – the software will detect it automatically VIFs for multicollinearity (less than 10 is good) vif Independence (No Autocorrelation) Durbin-Watson test and Lagrange Multiplier test estat dwatson estat bgodfrey, lags(p) 𝜀~𝑁0, 𝑎: The error term is normally distributed with a zero mean Histograms, Q-Q plots, or tests like the Shapiro-Wilk test histogram qnorm sktest

title: Exercises
text: Exercises 1. Open “Lectures 4&5 Data.xlsx” in a software of your choice. Estimate the following regression model by using the rental market data only. 2. Generate the predicted values and residuals from the regression model. 3. Generate scatter plots between the residual series and the predicted values. Does the pattern appear to be random? 4. Generate a histogram of the residuals. Does it seem to be normally distributed? Performa a Q-Q test to double check the results. 5. Perform a RESET test to check if any higher order terms or interaction terms of the independent variables are missing from the regression model. 6. Request VIF statistics to check the level of multicollinearity. Is there any concern? 7. Perform a White test to check the homoskedasticity assumption. Request the Robust Standard Errors if the model does not pass the test.
